findings.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:31 — Denial key joins name and parent with "_", which is also legal in dashboard/folder UIDs, so (name=a_b, folder=c) and (name=a, folder=b_c) share one key; a real denial on one resource then wrongly denies an allowed resource for the whole TTL, and because the denial cache is read before the positive cache, fresh grants can't override it

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — The denial key has no identity type, only the raw UserUID; anonymous and render-service subjects both use ID "0", so an anonymous denial (e.g. dashboards:read on X) is served to the renderer for the same name/folder, breaking image rendering of dashboards anonymous users can't see

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:139 — Removing the permCache read from getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions means every Check that the cached perms deny re-queries the permission DB, once per unique (name,folder); filtering N inaccessible resources now costs N DB queries instead of 1 cached lookup, and the in-proc client no longer has its 30s result cache (NoopCache) to absorb this

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:154 — Denial entries are keyed by caller-supplied name/folder with no size limit (LocalCache has no bound), so a client sending Checks with random or very long names makes one DB query and adds one cache entry per request, growing memory and DB load

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:982 — "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" seeds permCache with dash1:false (a deny, despite the "Allow" comment) and the default fakeStore returns no permissions, so the test still passes if the denial cache is removed or never consulted

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:153 — Nothing invalidates the new denial cache, and it is checked before any fresh lookup; if a Check reads the DB just before a grant and writes the denial just after, the stale denial wins for the full TTL, even after the positive permCache has been refreshed with the grant

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:137 — permissionCacheUsage is now recorded for renderer and anonymous requests; the renderer path always returns ErrNotFound and is counted as a cache miss, and denial-cache hits are counted as permCache hits, so the hit-rate metric is skewed
pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — Denial cache key omits identity type, so a cached denial for anonymous:0 is returned for render:0 (and vice versa), wrongly denying renderer dashboard reads.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:31 — Denial key joins name and parent with unescaped "_" so distinct (name, folder) pairs like ("a_b","c") and ("a","b_c") collide and one resource's denial is served for another.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:342 — getCachedIdentityPermissions duplicates getIdentityPermissions' identity-type switch and key derivation (anon/user key builders, GetUserIdentifiers call), so adding a new identity type or changing a cache key now has to be done in two parallel switches that can silently drift

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:379 — getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions now write permCache but no longer read it, so the cache-read responsibility is split between Check/List and the getters; any other or future caller of getIdentityPermissions silently skips the cache and always hits the DB

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:123 — getCachedIdentityPermissions returns cache.ErrNotFound for a miss and also passes through real errors (GetUserIdentifiers failures, unsupported identity type), and Check/List treat every error as a miss, so real failures are swallowed and repeated in getIdentityPermissions

pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30 — userPermDenialCacheKey uses the same ".perm_" prefix as userPermCacheKey/anonymousPermCacheKey and joins name/parent with "_" without escaping, so keys for two different value types in one shared cache can overlap (e.g. name "a_b"+parent "" equals name "a"+parent "b"); it is also named "user" but gets the raw checkReq.UserUID for every identity type, while the perm key uses the resolved UID

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:118 — The permissionCacheUsage/requestCount metric pairs are copy-pasted across the denial-hit, cached-allow and DB paths in Check (and again in List), and a cached-but-denied lookup is counted as a cache miss, so cache metrics are hard to read and easy to break when the flow changes

pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:239 — NoopCache is exported from the authz package even though it is only used in this package, uses a copied receiver name `lc` (from LocalCache), sits at the bottom of the file after an unrelated round-tripper, and has no comment explaining why the in-process client turns caching off

pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:160 — Removing the newRBACClient helper inlines two separate authzlib.NewClient builders that repeat the tracer option, and leaves a redundant `client :=` temp before `return client, nil

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:139 — Every Check denied by warm cached perms now falls through to getIdentityPermissions, which no longer reads permCache, so each distinct denied (name,parent) runs a fresh permission-store DB query (N denied items in a filtered listing means N DB queries every 30s, where before it was 0).

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — The denial cache is keyed per name/parent, so requests for unique or nonexistent resource names (including anonymous traffic) always miss it and each one triggers a DB permission query, turning attacker-controlled names into DB load amplification.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:154 — The negative cache adds one entry per user x action x name x parent to the shared LocalCache (30s TTL, but expired items are only purged by the 10-minute janitor), so entry count and memory grow without bound as unique names come in.

pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:103 — Switching the in-process client to NoopCache drops its 30s Check/List result cache, so every authz call now goes through inprocgrpc marshaling, identity lookup, JSON-decoding of the full permission map (and folder tree), and List recomputation.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:125 — On the deny path checkPermission runs twice (cached perms, then DB perms), so GetUserIdentifiers runs twice and buildFolderTree JSON-decodes the whole namespace folder tree from cache twice per request.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:137 — Every cached-perm deny for a new (user, action, name, folder) tuple now bypasses permCache and forces a full DB permission reload (getUserPermissions no longer reads permCache), so fan-out denied checks (e.g. per-dashboard checks) turn into N DB queries where there used to be 0, which can amplify DB load under normal traffic

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:123 — getCachedIdentityPermissions errors (GetUserIdentifiers DB failure, unsupported identity type) are discarded without logging and the same failing DB lookup runs again in getIdentityPermissions (service.go:374), doubling DB queries per request during a DB outage

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:154 — permDenialCache keys have unbounded cardinality (per user x action x name x parent folder) and live in a local cache whose expired entries are only purged every 10 minutes, so memory can grow a lot under high-cardinality denied traffic

pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:103 — Switching the in-process client to NoopCache drops the 30s client-side result cache, so every in-process Check/List now reaches the server, and combined with the deny fall-through that raises per-request DB load

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:125 — A checkPermission error on the stale cached-perm path (e.g. a transient buildFolderTree failure) returns an error right away instead of falling through to fresh permissions, which might grant directly without needing the folder lookup

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:137 — permissionCacheUsage now also counts anonymous and render-service requests (renderer is never cached, so it is always a miss), counts cache-lookup errors as misses, and counts denial-cache hits as permission-cache hits, which changes hit-ratio metric semantics that dashboards and alerts rely on

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:117 — The denial cache is checked before any permission data and is never cleared when permCache is refreshed with a grant, so a newly granted permission can still be denied for up to shortCacheTTL even after fresh perms were loaded by another request

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:153 — Denial cache stores one entry per caller-influenced (user, action, name, folder) tuple in the shared in-memory LocalCache (10-min cleanup interval), so a low-privileged user issuing denied checks for many distinct/random resource names can grow server memory without bound.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30 — userPermDenialCacheKey joins name and parent with unescaped "_" (e.g. name "a_b"/parent "" vs name "a"/parent "b"), so a denial for one resource is served for a different resource the user is actually allowed to access (false deny).

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — Denial key omits identity type and uses the raw subject ID rather than the resolved user UID, so anonymous/render/user/service-account subjects with the same raw ID string share denial entries and can wrongly deny each other.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:117 — Denial cache is checked before and independently of permCache with no invalidation, so a newly granted permission stays denied for up to shortCacheTTL (30s) even after permCache is refreshed.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:982 — "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" seeds permCache with dash1=false (the comment says "Allow") and the default fakeStore has no permissions, so it still denies if the permDenialCache lookup is removed; the test proves nothing about the denial cache

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:154 — No test covers denial-cache population or staleness: nothing checks that a DB deny writes permDenialCache, or that a permission granted later stays masked by the cached deny for up to shortCacheTTL

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — The denial key has no identity type (only raw UserUID), so anonymous:0 and render:0 share a key and an anonymous deny can override the renderer's wildcard allow; no test covers identity-type isolation for denials

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:947 — The cache-first tests never check store/identityStore call counts or that the cache was refreshed, so they don't show whether the DB was skipped on a hit or re-queried on a cache-only deny

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:347 — The new cache-first branches in getCachedIdentityPermissions for anonymous, service-account and render are untested; the anonymous and render Check/List tests only hit the cache-miss path

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:1291 — TestService_CacheList only covers a cache hit; it has no test that List serves stale cached perms with no DB fallback (a new grant stays missing until TTL), and no test for the cache-miss metrics/error path

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:337 — The cache-hit case was removed from TestService_getUserPermissions but the cacheHit field and its `if tc.cacheHit` branches remain as dead code; no test was added asserting getIdentityPermissions now always goes to the store
pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:239 — NoopCache and the in-process client switch to no client-side cache have no tests (e.g. Get returns cache.ErrNotFound, and repeated in-process Checks reach the server)

pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30 — No test checks the uniqueness of userPermDenialCacheKey: "_"-joined name/parent can collide (name "a_b",parent "c" vs name "a",parent "b_c"), and the key extends the userPermCacheKey prefix in the same shared cache

goldens.comment: The Check operation exhibits asymmetric cache trust logic: cached permission grants are trusted and returned immediately, but cached denials from the same permission cache are ignored, leading to a fresh database lookup. This allows stale cached grants to provide access to revoked resources, posing a security risk.
The test comment says the cached permissions 'allow access', but the map stores false for dashboards:uid:dash1, so checkPermission will still treat this scope as not allowed.

The cache key construction in `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses simple string concatenation with underscores, which can lead to ambiguous keys and collision risks when any component contains underscores or is empty. This could result in incorrect denial cache hits, affecting user permissions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — The denial key has no identity type, only the raw UserUID; anonymous and render-service subjects both use ID "0", so an anonymous denial (e.g. dashboards:read on X) is served to the renderer for the same name/folder, breaking image rendering of dashboards anonymous users can't see

adjudication.rationale: In `Service.Check`, the new `permDenialKey` is computed as `userPermDenialCacheKey(namespace, checkReq.UserUID, action, name, parentFolder)` and is checked *before* any branching on `checkReq.IdentityType` (`permDenialCache.Get` happens before `getCachedIdentityPermissions`). The denial key does not include `IdentityType` (or full `Subject`), so different identity types that share the same `UserUID` string would collide and could incorrectly reuse a cached denial across subjects. However, the finding’s specific claim that anonymous and render-service both use user UID "0" is not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:139 — Removing the permCache read from getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions means every Check that the cached perms deny re-queries the permission DB, once per unique (name,folder); filtering N inaccessible resources now costs N DB queries instead of 1 cached lookup, and the in-proc client no longer has its 30s result cache (NoopCache) to absorb this

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the permCache read paths from getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions (service.go: getUserPermissions and getAnonymousPermissions no longer early-return cached results), and Check now only returns early on a cache hit when checkPermission yields Allowed=true; if cached permissions deny (allowed=false), it falls through to getIdentityPermissions (DB) unless a permDenialCache entry exists for that specific (namespace,user,action,name,parentFolder) key (service.go: new permDenialKey logic and Set on !allowed). This makes negative checks potentially trigger DB queries once per unique (name,parentFolder) until the explicit denial cache is populated, which is a real performance/architecture concern but not a correctness defect. Separately, ProvideAuthZClient now constructs an in-proc authzlib client with a NoopCache (rbac.go), eliminating the previous local-cache client behavior for that path, which further supports the stated performance impact.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:154 — Denial entries are keyed by caller-supplied name/folder with no size limit (LocalCache has no bound), so a client sending Checks with random or very long names makes one DB query and adds one cache entry per request, growing memory and DB load

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `permDenialCache` and unconditionally caches denials keyed by `checkReq.Name` and `checkReq.ParentFolder` (`permDenialKey := userPermDenialCacheKey(..., checkReq.Name, checkReq.ParentFolder)`; `if !allowed { s.permDenialCache.Set(ctx, permDenialKey, true) }`). Those fields come from the request and can vary arbitrarily, so a client can generate many unique denial keys (including very long strings), creating many cache entries. The shown LocalCache usage/configuration in this PR is purely TTL-based (e.g., `cache.NewLocalCache(cache.Config{Expiry: ..., CleanupInterval: ...})`) with no demonstrated size bound in the diff, so this can cause unbounded memory growth over the TTL window and extra per-request allocations; each unique miss still triggers the DB permission fetch before the denial is cached.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:982 — "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" seeds permCache with dash1:false (a deny, despite the "Allow" comment) and the default fakeStore returns no permissions, so the test still passes if the denial cache is removed or never consulted
matched_golden_ids: The test comment says the cached permissions 'allow access', but the map stores false for dashboards:uid:dash1, so checkPermission will still treat this scope as not allowed.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that the test comment/intent implies cached permissions should allow access, but the cache is seeded with dash1:false (a deny). This means checkPermission would treat that scope as not allowed, and the test may not actually validate the intended allow-from-cache behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:153 — Nothing invalidates the new denial cache, and it is checked before any fresh lookup; if a Check reads the DB just before a grant and writes the denial just after, the stale denial wins for the full TTL, even after the positive permCache has been refreshed with the grant

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check, a permDenialCache entry is consulted first (early return false) via userPermDenialCacheKey(...) before any cached-permissions check or DB lookup. The code only ever writes denial entries (if !allowed { s.permDenialCache.Set(...) }) and never clears them on later allows or permission changes; thus a cached denial can cause false negatives until shortCacheTTL expires, even if permissions are later granted and permCache is refreshed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:137 — permissionCacheUsage is now recorded for renderer and anonymous requests; the renderer path always returns ErrNotFound and is counted as a cache miss, and denial-cache hits are counted as permCache hits, so the hit-rate metric is skewed

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Check` now increments `permissionCacheUsage` on a `permDenialCache` hit (`WithLabelValues("true", ...)`), which will be indistinguishable from a real permission-cache hit and can skew the hit-rate metric. Also, `getCachedIdentityPermissions` hardcodes `types.TypeRenderService` to `return nil, cache.ErrNotFound`, and both `Check` and `List` treat any non-nil error as a cache miss and increment `permissionCacheUsage` with `"false"`, so render-service requests will always be counted as misses. This impacts metrics/observability but not authorization correctness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — Denial cache key omits identity type, so a cached denial for anonymous:0 is returned for render:0 (and vice versa), wrongly denying renderer dashboard reads.

adjudication.rationale: In `Service.Check`, the denial cache is consulted using `permDenialKey := userPermDenialCacheKey(checkReq.Namespace.Value, checkReq.UserUID, checkReq.Action, checkReq.Name, checkReq.ParentFolder)` and `userPermDenialCacheKey` only incorporates `namespace`, `userUID`, `action`, `name`, and `parent` (no `IdentityType`). Since the check occurs before any identity-type-specific handling, a denial cached for one identity type can be incorrectly applied to another identity type that shares the same `UserUID` value, causing wrong denials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:31 — Denial key joins name and parent with unescaped "_" so distinct (name, folder) pairs like ("a_b","c") and ("a","b_c") collide and one resource's denial is served for another.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `userPermDenialCacheKey(namespace, userUID, action, name, parent)` which builds the cache key by string-concatenating components with "_" separators: `... + "_" + name + "_" + parent` (pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go). Since neither `name` nor `parent` are escaped/length-delimited, different `(name,parent)` pairs that contain underscores can produce the same final key, causing a denial cached for one resource to be reused for another. This key is then used for early deny in `Service.Check` via `permDenialCache.Get`, so a collision would produce incorrect authorization decisions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:342 — getCachedIdentityPermissions duplicates getIdentityPermissions' identity-type switch and key derivation (anon/user key builders, GetUserIdentifiers call), so adding a new identity type or changing a cache key now has to be done in two parallel switches that can silently drift

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `getCachedIdentityPermissions(...)` with an `identity-type` switch that derives cache keys (`anonymousPermCacheKey`, `userPermCacheKey`) and calls `GetUserIdentifiers` for user/service-account paths. The existing `getIdentityPermissions(...)` (already present in the file, and still used as the fallback in `Check`/`List`) necessarily also branches on `IdentityType` to decide how to fetch permissions (anon vs user vs render service, etc.). This creates two parallel identity-type decision points for the same concept (permission lookup), and key-derivation logic now lives in this new helper in addition to the lower-level permission functions. That’s a maintainability/architecture concern (risk of drift when adding identity types or changing cache key rules), but it’s not a verifiable runtime defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:379 — getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions now write permCache but no longer read it, so the cache-read responsibility is split between Check/List and the getters; any other or future caller of getIdentityPermissions silently skips the cache and always hits the DB

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes permCache read paths inside getUserPermissions and getAnonymousPermissions (the permCache.Get blocks are deleted), while those functions still populate permCache via Set after fetching from the store. Cache reads are now performed explicitly in Check and List via the new getCachedIdentityPermissions helper. This splits caching responsibility across call sites and makes getIdentityPermissions effectively “uncached” (it will always hit store paths when called), which is a real maintainability/architecture concern and could surprise any other current/future caller of getIdentityPermissions that expects caching there. The diff alone doesn’t prove there is another caller today, so it’s not a verifiable functional bug from the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:123 — getCachedIdentityPermissions returns cache.ErrNotFound for a miss and also passes through real errors (GetUserIdentifiers failures, unsupported identity type), and Check/List treat every error as a miss, so real failures are swallowed and repeated in getIdentityPermissions

adjudication.rationale: In both `Check` and `List`, the code only uses cached permissions when `getCachedIdentityPermissions(...)` returns `err == nil`; otherwise it proceeds to fetch via `getIdentityPermissions` (Check: after the `if err == nil { ... }` block; List: `else { ... permissions, err = s.getIdentityPermissions(...) }`). Since `getCachedIdentityPermissions` can return non-`cache.ErrNotFound` errors (e.g., `GetUserIdentifiers` failure or `unsupported identity type`), those errors are not surfaced at the cache stage and instead trigger a second attempt via `getIdentityPermissions`, potentially duplicating work and obscuring the original failure. However, the request still fails if the underlying issue persists (because `getIdentityPermissions` will likely error too), so this is more of an error-handling/clarity/perf concern than a clear correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30 — userPermDenialCacheKey uses the same ".perm_" prefix as userPermCacheKey/anonymousPermCacheKey and joins name/parent with "_" without escaping, so keys for two different value types in one shared cache can overlap (e.g. name "a_b"+parent "" equals name "a"+parent "b"); it is also named "user" but gets the raw checkReq.UserUID for every identity type, while the perm key uses the resolved UID

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go the new userPermDenialCacheKey builds a cache key by concatenating variable fields (action, name, parent) with '_' separators and without escaping/length-prefixing. This can produce identical keys for different (name,parent) pairs (e.g., name="a_b", parent="" vs name="a", parent="b"), causing incorrect cache hits and thus incorrect authorization denials. The diff also shows permDenialKey is built from checkReq.UserUID directly (service.go) while the normal permission cache key uses the resolved userIdentifiers.UID in getCachedIdentityPermissions, which is a concrete inconsistency that can lead to denial-cache misses or mixing if UserUID is not the canonical UID.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:118 — The permissionCacheUsage/requestCount metric pairs are copy-pasted across the denial-hit, cached-allow and DB paths in Check (and again in List), and a cached-but-denied lookup is counted as a cache miss, so cache metrics are hard to read and easy to break when the flow changes

adjudication.rationale: In `Service.Check`, there are multiple copy-pasted metric increments across distinct branches (permDenialCache hit, cached allow, error path, DB path): e.g. early deny-hit does `permissionCacheUsage.WithLabelValues("true", ...)` + `requestCount...`, cached-allow does the same, and later the non-cached/DB path increments separately. Also, if `getCachedIdentityPermissions` returns cached perms but `checkPermission` returns `allowed == false`, the code falls through and then unconditionally does `permissionCacheUsage.WithLabelValues("false", checkReq.Action).Inc()`, so a cached-but-denied result is counted as a cache miss (hard to interpret). `List` similarly adds a cache-hit/miss metric branch around `getCachedIdentityPermissions` vs `getIdentityPermissions`, duplicating the pattern. This is a diff-grounded metrics/maintainability issue rather than a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:239 — NoopCache is exported from the authz package even though it is only used in this package, uses a copied receiver name `lc` (from LocalCache), sits at the bottom of the file after an unrelated round-tripper, and has no comment explaining why the in-process client turns caching off

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `type NoopCache struct{}` in `pkg/services/authz/rbac.go` (exported via capitalization) and it is only referenced in this diff when constructing the in-process client in `ProvideAuthZClient` via `authzlib.WithCacheClientOption(&NoopCache{})`. It is placed at the end of `rbac.go` after the unrelated `tokenExhangeRoundTripper` code and has no comment explaining why caching is intentionally disabled for the in-process client. The method receivers use `lc`, which appears inconsistent with the type name and looks like a carryover from `LocalCache`. These are maintainability/style/documentation issues rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:160 — Removing the newRBACClient helper inlines two separate authzlib.NewClient builders that repeat the tracer option, and leaves a redundant `client :=` temp before `return client, nil

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show two separate `authzlib.NewClient(..., authzlib.WithTracerClientOption(tracer))` call sites (in `ProvideAuthZClient` and `newRemoteRBACClient`) and `newRemoteRBACClient` uses a temporary `client := ...` before `return client, nil`. However, this is a refactor/style/duplication nit rather than a verifiable defect or substantive review issue grounded in behavior (the two call sites intentionally differ in cache options: `NoopCache{}` vs `cache.NewLocalCache(...)`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:139 — Every Check denied by warm cached perms now falls through to getIdentityPermissions, which no longer reads permCache, so each distinct denied (name,parent) runs a fresh permission-store DB query (N denied items in a filtered listing means N DB queries every 30s, where before it was 0).

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Service.Check` to only short-circuit on cached *allows*: it calls `getCachedIdentityPermissions(...)`, runs `checkPermission(...)`, and returns early only when `allowed` is true (new block around `service.go` ~lines 113-141). If the cached permissions do not allow the конкрет `(name,parent)` check, it always falls through to `getIdentityPermissions(...)`, which ultimately queries the store. At the same time, `getUserPermissions`/`getAnonymousPermissions` no longer read `permCache` directly (cache reads were removed), so this fallback is a real extra DB hit path. While the newly added `permDenialCache` can prevent repeated DB queries for the *same* denied `(namespace,user,action,name,parent)` combination, the first denial for each distinct item will still query the DB even when `permCache` is warm. This is a diff-grounded performance regression/behavior change, not a correctness defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — The denial cache is keyed per name/parent, so requests for unique or nonexistent resource names (including anonymous traffic) always miss it and each one triggers a DB permission query, turning attacker-controlled names into DB load amplification.

adjudication.rationale: In `Service.Check`, cached permissions are only used to short-circuit when they allow (`if allowed { return ... }`), but when cached permissions deny, the code falls through to `getIdentityPermissions(...)` (DB-backed) every time unless `permDenialCache` hits. The denial cache key is `namespace + userUID + action + name + parent` (`userPermDenialCacheKey(...)`), so varying `Name`/`ParentFolder` produces consistent cache misses and repeated DB permission fetches. Since `Name`/`Folder` are request-controlled fields, this creates a diff-introduced, attacker-amplifiable DB load path (the denial cache doesn't mitigate unique/nonexistent names).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:154 — The negative cache adds one entry per user x action x name x parent to the shared LocalCache (30s TTL, but expired items are only purged by the 10-minute janitor), so entry count and memory grow without bound as unique names come in.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new negative cache keyed by namespace+userUID+action+name+parent (`userPermDenialCacheKey(...)`) and populates it on deny (`s.permDenialCache.Set(ctx, permDenialKey, true)` in `Service.Check`). That can introduce high-cardinality cache keys (one per unique resource name/parent), which may drive up cache size between expirations/cleanups. However, the finding’s specific claim about a “shared LocalCache (30s TTL, 10-minute janitor)” is not verifiable for `permDenialCache` from this diff: the 30s/10m config shown is for the *client* cache in `newRemoteRBACClient`, while the service’s underlying cache config/cleanup behavior isn’t shown here. So it’s a grounded performance/scaling concern, but not a provable defect with the stated TTL/janitor details.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:103 — Switching the in-process client to NoopCache drops its 30s Check/List result cache, so every authz call now goes through inprocgrpc marshaling, identity lookup, JSON-decoding of the full permission map (and folder tree), and List recomputation.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes the in-process RBAC client construction in ProvideAuthZClient from newRBACClient(channel, tracer) (which configured authzlib.NewClient with a real local cache: cache.NewLocalCache with 30s expiry in newRemoteRBACClient/newRBACClient) to authzlib.NewClient(..., authzlib.WithCacheClientOption(&NoopCache{}), ...). NoopCache.Get always returns cache.ErrNotFound, so client-side caching is effectively disabled for in-process calls. This is a concrete performance/behavioral change (more calls flow through the inproc gRPC path), though not a correctness defect. The extra specifics about JSON-decoding/folder tree recomputation are plausible but not directly verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:125 — On the deny path checkPermission runs twice (cached perms, then DB perms), so GetUserIdentifiers runs twice and buildFolderTree JSON-decodes the whole namespace folder tree from cache twice per request.

adjudication.rationale: In `Service.Check`, the new fast-path calls `checkPermission` using `cachedPerms` (via `getCachedIdentityPermissions`) and only returns early when `allowed` is true (service.go: new block before `getIdentityPermissions`). If cached permissions exist but do not allow the request, the code falls through, calls `getIdentityPermissions(...)` and then calls `checkPermission(...)` again on the DB-derived permissions (existing logic after `getIdentityPermissions`). For user/service-account identities, `getCachedIdentityPermissions` calls `s.GetUserIdentifiers(...)` and `getIdentityPermissions` will later call `getUserPermissions(...)`, which also calls `s.GetUserIdentifiers(...)` (see `getUserPermissions` in the diff). That duplicated work is a real performance concern introduced by this change, but it’s not a correctness defect. The claim about `buildFolderTree` JSON-decoding twice is not verifiable from this diff because `checkPermission`/folder-tree internals aren’t shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:137 — Every cached-perm deny for a new (user, action, name, folder) tuple now bypasses permCache and forces a full DB permission reload (getUserPermissions no longer reads permCache), so fan-out denied checks (e.g. per-dashboard checks) turn into N DB queries where there used to be 0, which can amplify DB load under normal traffic

adjudication.rationale: In `Service.Check`, the new flow only returns early when the cached permission check is **allowed**. If `getCachedIdentityPermissions` hits `permCache` but `checkPermission` returns `allowed == false`, the code falls through and calls `getIdentityPermissions` anyway (i.e., forces a fresh permission load) before setting `permDenialCache` for that specific (user,action,name,parent) key. Additionally, `getUserPermissions`/`getAnonymousPermissions` no longer read `s.permCache` at the start (those cache-hit branches were removed), so this fallthrough cannot reuse the already-cached permission map and will drive the DB/store path for each new denied tuple until `permDenialCache` is populated. This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/DB-load concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:123 — getCachedIdentityPermissions errors (GetUserIdentifiers DB failure, unsupported identity type) are discarded without logging and the same failing DB lookup runs again in getIdentityPermissions (service.go:374), doubling DB queries per request during a DB outage

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check (and similarly List), the new pre-check `getCachedIdentityPermissions(...)` is called and its `err` is ignored unless `err == nil` (no logging/handling). For user/service-account identities, `getCachedIdentityPermissions` calls `s.GetUserIdentifiers(...)` and may hit the DB; on failure it returns an error, but Check then proceeds to call `getIdentityPermissions(...)`, which (via `getUserPermissions`) will call `GetUserIdentifiers` again. This can duplicate the same failing DB lookup per request during an outage. It’s a diff-grounded resiliency/performance concern rather than a direct correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:154 — permDenialCache keys have unbounded cardinality (per user x action x name x parent folder) and live in a local cache whose expired entries are only purged every 10 minutes, so memory can grow a lot under high-cardinality denied traffic

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new negative-result cache `permDenialCache` keyed by `namespace + userUID + action + name + parent` (see `userPermDenialCacheKey(...)` in `cache.go` and its use in `Service.Check` where `permDenialCache.Set(...)` is called on denied checks). This key space is high/unbounded cardinality under denied traffic across many resource names/folders, so it can drive significant in-memory growth in whatever backing cache implementation is used. However, the finding’s specific claim about expired entries only being purged every 10 minutes is not shown in this diff (cleanup/purge interval isn’t visible here), so that part cannot be verified from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:103 — Switching the in-process client to NoopCache drops the 30s client-side result cache, so every in-process Check/List now reaches the server, and combined with the deny fall-through that raises per-request DB load

adjudication.rationale: The diff does switch the in-process RBAC client from `newRBACClient(channel, tracer)` (which used a 30s `cache.NewLocalCache`) to `authzlib.NewClient(..., authzlib.WithCacheClientOption(&NoopCache{}), ...)`, which effectively disables client-side caching for in-process calls. That means more in-process Check/List requests will reach the server handler instead of being served from the client cache. Separately, `Service.Check` now falls through to `getIdentityPermissions` (DB-backed) when cached permissions exist but do not allow the request, which can increase DB load compared to a pure “deny from cached perms” behavior. This is a concrete performance/architecture regression risk grounded in the diff, not a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:125 — A checkPermission error on the stale cached-perm path (e.g. a transient buildFolderTree failure) returns an error right away instead of falling through to fresh permissions, which might grant directly without needing the folder lookup

adjudication.rationale: In `Service.Check`, when cached permissions are found (`getCachedIdentityPermissions` returns `err == nil`), the code calls `s.checkPermission(ctx, cachedPerms, checkReq)` and if that returns an error it immediately returns `deny, err` (see the new block around `// could not check permission`). Unlike the later non-cached path, there is no attempt to fall back to `getIdentityPermissions(...)` and re-check. This means a transient/edge error triggered while evaluating cached perms can cause the request to fail even though a fresh permissions fetch might succeed and allow the request. This is a behavior regression introduced by the new cache-fast-path logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:137 — permissionCacheUsage now also counts anonymous and render-service requests (renderer is never cached, so it is always a miss), counts cache-lookup errors as misses, and counts denial-cache hits as permission-cache hits, which changes hit-ratio metric semantics that dashboards and alerts rely on

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `permissionCacheUsage` semantics changed. In `Service.Check`, a `permDenialCache` hit increments `permissionCacheUsage` with hit=`true` ("true", action) before returning a deny, so denial-cache hits are counted as permission-cache hits (service.go: new block around `permDenialKey`). Also, `getCachedIdentityPermissions` is now used by both `Check` and `List`, and it handles `TypeAnonymous` (can be hit/miss) and forces `TypeRenderService` to return `cache.ErrNotFound` (always counted as a miss via `permissionCacheUsage.WithLabelValues("false", ...)` in `Check` and `List`). Finally, any error from `getCachedIdentityPermissions` (including non-cache errors like `GetUserIdentifiers` failure) results in the miss counter being incremented, conflating lookup errors with misses. This is a real, diff-grounded monitoring/metrics contract concern rather than a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:117 — The denial cache is checked before any permission data and is never cleared when permCache is refreshed with a grant, so a newly granted permission can still be denied for up to shortCacheTTL even after fresh perms were loaded by another request

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check(), the new permDenialCache is consulted first and immediately returns Allowed:false on a hit (service.go around the added block using userPermDenialCacheKey + s.permDenialCache.Get). Denial entries are added when a DB-backed check yields !allowed (s.permDenialCache.Set(...) after getIdentityPermissions/checkPermission). There is no code in the diff that clears or bypasses this denial cache when permissions are later reloaded/updated to allow (e.g., permCache may now contain a grant, but the denial cache is checked before cachedPerms are evaluated). Therefore, a previously cached denial can incorrectly override a newly granted permission for up to shortCacheTTL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:153 — Denial cache stores one entry per caller-influenced (user, action, name, folder) tuple in the shared in-memory LocalCache (10-min cleanup interval), so a low-privileged user issuing denied checks for many distinct/random resource names can grow server memory without bound.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `permDenialCache` and stores a denial entry on any failed check (`if !allowed { s.permDenialCache.Set(ctx, permDenialKey, true) }`). The cache key is built from caller-controlled fields (`userPermDenialCacheKey(namespace, userUID, action, name, parent)`), so a user can trigger many unique denies by varying `Name`/`Folder` (and thus the key). There’s no bounding/eviction logic shown beyond TTL, so memory can grow significantly within the TTL window (and until cleanup), creating a resource-exhaustion/DoS risk attributable to this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30 — userPermDenialCacheKey joins name and parent with unescaped "_" (e.g. name "a_b"/parent "" vs name "a"/parent "b"), so a denial for one resource is served for a different resource the user is actually allowed to access (false deny).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `userPermDenialCacheKey(namespace, userUID, action, name, parent)` which concatenates fields with raw underscores: `... + "_" + name + "_" + parent`. If `name` and/or `parent` can contain `_`, different (name,parent) pairs can map to the same cache key (e.g., name="a_b", parent="c" vs name="a", parent="b_c"), and because `Service.Check` short-circuits to deny on any `permDenialCache` hit, such a collision would cause an incorrect deny. However, the finding’s specific example (name "a_b"/parent "" vs name "a"/parent "b") does not actually collide due to the trailing underscore, and the diff does not show what characters `name`/`parent` may contain, so this cannot be confirmed as an always-real defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — Denial key omits identity type and uses the raw subject ID rather than the resolved user UID, so anonymous/render/user/service-account subjects with the same raw ID string share denial entries and can wrongly deny each other.

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check, the denial cache key is computed as `userPermDenialCacheKey(checkReq.Namespace.Value, checkReq.UserUID, checkReq.Action, checkReq.Name, checkReq.ParentFolder)` and checked before any identity-type-specific handling or UID resolution. The key function includes no identity type discriminator, so different subject types that populate `checkReq.UserUID` with the same string would share denial entries. Also, unlike permission caching (which for users/service accounts resolves `userIdentifiers.UID` via `GetUserIdentifiers` in `getCachedIdentityPermissions`), the denial key uses `checkReq.UserUID` directly, so it can diverge from the canonical UID used elsewhere, leading to incorrect cross-subject denial or inconsistent caching behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:117 — Denial cache is checked before and independently of permCache with no invalidation, so a newly granted permission stays denied for up to shortCacheTTL (30s) even after permCache is refreshed.

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check, the new permDenialCache is consulted first and causes an immediate deny (`if _, ok := s.permDenialCache.Get(...); ok { return Allowed:false }`) before checking permCache or querying the store. Later, denials are added (`if !allowed { s.permDenialCache.Set(..., true) }`) but there is no corresponding deletion/invalidation when permissions change or when an allow is observed. Because this denial check is independent of permCache and runs first, a previously cached denial will override newly cached/updated allowed permissions until the denial entry expires (shortCacheTTL).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:982 — "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" seeds permCache with dash1=false (the comment says "Allow") and the default fakeStore has no permissions, so it still denies if the permDenialCache lookup is removed; the test proves nothing about the denial cache

adjudication.rationale: In `TestService_CacheCheck` subtest "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry", the setup seeds `permDenialCache` but also sets `permCache` for `dashboards:uid:dash1` to `false` (despite the comment saying it’s to "Allow"). In `Service.Check`, cached permissions are consulted next (`getCachedIdentityPermissions` + `checkPermission`), and an `allowed==false` result does not short-circuit; it falls through to the DB path, which (with the default fake store/empty permissions) will also deny. Therefore, even if the `permDenialCache` fast-path were removed, the test would still deny, so it doesn’t actually prove the denial-cache behavior. This is a test-quality issue grounded in the diff, not a product defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:154 — No test covers denial-cache population or staleness: nothing checks that a DB deny writes permDenialCache, or that a permission granted later stays masked by the cached deny for up to shortCacheTTL

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new denial-cache behavior in Service.Check: it looks up permDenialCache first (early return deny) and, after a DB-backed permission evaluation, populates the denial cache when `!allowed` (`s.permDenialCache.Set(ctx, permDenialKey, true)`). The new tests cover an explicit pre-seeded denial entry ("Should deny on explicit cache deny entry") and cache-allow / DB fallback scenarios, but none verify that a DB denial actually writes into `permDenialCache`, nor that a later-allowed permission would still be denied due to a previously cached deny until shortCacheTTL expires. That is a specific, diff-grounded gap in test coverage for the newly introduced logic, not an already-proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — The denial key has no identity type (only raw UserUID), so anonymous:0 and render:0 share a key and an anonymous deny can override the renderer's wildcard allow; no test covers identity-type isolation for denials

adjudication.rationale: The new denial-cache short-circuit in `Service.Check` builds `permDenialKey` from `namespace`, `checkReq.UserUID`, `action`, `name`, and `parentFolder` only (`userPermDenialCacheKey(...)`), and does not include `checkReq.IdentityType` (see `service.go` around the new `permDenialKey := ...` block). That means denials are not explicitly isolated by identity type, so different identity types that can share the same `UserUID` string could collide and incorrectly reuse a deny entry. The added tests cover user-based allow/miss/outdated and an explicit deny, but do not cover cross-identity-type isolation for the new denial cache logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:947 — The cache-first tests never check store/identityStore call counts or that the cache was refreshed, so they don't show whether the DB was skipped on a hit or re-queried on a cache-only deny

adjudication.rationale: The newly added cache-first tests (e.g., `TestService_CacheCheck` and `TestService_CacheList`) assert outcomes (Allowed/Denied, listed items) but do not assert whether the underlying stores were or were not invoked. For example, the "Allow based on cached permissions" case sets `idCache`/`permCache` and expects `Allowed`, but it would still pass even if `Check` incorrectly queried `s.permissionStore`/`s.store` because there are no call-count assertions. Similarly, the explicit deny-cache case returns early on `permDenialCache.Get(...)`, but the test does not verify that DB/identityStore were skipped. This is a concrete gap in validating the intended cache-fast-path behavior introduced in the diff, not a functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:347 — The new cache-first branches in getCachedIdentityPermissions for anonymous, service-account and render are untested; the anonymous and render Check/List tests only hit the cache-miss path

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new cache-first helper `getCachedIdentityPermissions` with distinct behavior by identity type (anonymous cache lookup, render service forced miss, user/service-account cache lookup) and `Check`/`List` now depend on it. The newly added tests (`TestService_CacheCheck`, `TestService_CacheList`) only exercise the user path (`Subject: "user:test-uid"`) and do not cover the anonymous path (`types.TypeAnonymous`) or the service-account variant of the user/service-account branch. The finding’s wording about a “cache-first branch” for render is slightly off (render explicitly returns `cache.ErrNotFound`), and claims about existing anonymous/render tests can’t be verified from this diff, but the core issue—new identity-type branches lacking coverage—is grounded in the changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:1291 — TestService_CacheList only covers a cache hit; it has no test that List serves stale cached perms with no DB fallback (a new grant stays missing until TTL), and no test for the cache-miss metrics/error path

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `List` was changed to use `getCachedIdentityPermissions` first and only falls back to `getIdentityPermissions` on cache miss/error (see `Service.List`: it returns cached `permissions` when `err == nil`). That means if the cache contains an entry that is stale/incomplete (e.g., missing a newly granted scope), `List` will not query the DB until TTL expiry. The new `TestService_CacheList` added here only exercises the cache-hit path (prepopulated `permCache`) and does not cover (a) stale cached permissions causing missing results with no DB fallback, or (b) the cache-miss/fallback branch and its metrics/error behavior. This is a specific, diff-grounded test coverage gap for newly added nontrivial logic, not a directly verifiable functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:337 — The cache-hit case was removed from TestService_getUserPermissions but the cacheHit field and its `if tc.cacheHit` branches remain as dead code; no test was added asserting getIdentityPermissions now always goes to the store

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show the cache-hit test case being removed from `TestService_getUserPermissions`, but it does not show (or otherwise prove) that the `cacheHit` field and `if tc.cacheHit` branches still exist as dead code elsewhere in that test. Also, the change adds new cache-focused tests (`TestService_CacheCheck`, `TestService_CacheList`) that exercise cache-hit and fallback-to-store behavior at the service level, so the claim that no replacement test coverage was added is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:239 — NoopCache and the in-process client switch to no client-side cache have no tests (e.g. Get returns cache.ErrNotFound, and repeated in-process Checks reach the server)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `NoopCache` type in `pkg/services/authz/rbac.go` whose `Get` always returns `cache.ErrNotFound`, and wires it into the in-process client creation in `ProvideAuthZClient` via `authzlib.WithCacheClientOption(&NoopCache{})`, effectively disabling client-side caching for the in-process path. The added/modified tests (`TestService_CacheCheck`, `TestService_CacheList`) exercise server-side/service caching behavior (`permCache`, `permDenialCache`) but do not cover `NoopCache` itself nor verify the in-process client’s no-cache behavior (e.g., repeated checks causing repeated server calls). This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test concern, not a demonstrated functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30 — No test checks the uniqueness of userPermDenialCacheKey: "_"-joined name/parent can collide (name "a_b",parent "c" vs name "a",parent "b_c"), and the key extends the userPermCacheKey prefix in the same shared cache

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `userPermDenialCacheKey(namespace, userUID, action, name, parent)` implemented as simple underscore concatenation: `... + "_" + name + "_" + parent`. This scheme is not injective: different `(name,parent)` pairs can produce the same key when components may contain `_` (e.g., `("a_b","c")` vs `("a","b_c")`), which would cause `permDenialCache` lookups in `Service.Check` to incorrectly hit and deny access. The tests added exercise denial caching behavior but do not cover or prevent such key-collision scenarios.
